title: What Is a CRM?
learningGoal: Understand what a CRM does and why LeadProspectrr should be treated as one connected business system.

items.title: Customer Relationship Management
items.description: CRM stands for Customer Relationship Management. At its simplest, a CRM keeps track of the people and businesses you communicate with.

items.title: Questions a CRM Answers
items.description: Who is this person? How did they find us? What are they interested in? What have we sent them? Have they replied? Have they booked? What should happen next?

items.title: Contact List Stores Information
items.description: A contact list is just a database of names and details. It does not help you act on that information.

items.title: CRM Helps You Act
items.description: A CRM tracks conversations, appointments, tasks, notes, sales opportunities, tags, custom fields, documents, payments, and automated follow-up.

keyPoint: Every lead should have a clear next step. A CRM is not just storage—it is a system for action.

actionSteps.title: Think About Your Current System
actionSteps.description: How do you currently track leads? Spreadsheets? Sticky notes? Memory?

actionSteps.title: Identify Gaps
actionSteps.description: What information do you lose or forget between first contact and sale?

actionSteps.title: List Your Needs
actionSteps.description: Write down the top 3 things you need a CRM to help you track.

quizzes.question: What does CRM stand for?
quizzes.explanation: CRM stands for Customer Relationship Management. It is a system for managing interactions with current and potential customers.

quizzes.question: What is the difference between a contact list and a CRM?

options.option_text: A contact list stores information; a CRM helps you act on that information
CRMs do not store contact information

quizzes.explanation: A contact list is passive storage. A CRM actively helps you track interactions, automate follow-up, and manage the customer journey.

quizzes.question: What is the key rule of a working CRM?

options.option_text: Store as much data as possible
Every lead should have a clear next step

quizzes.explanation: The key rule is that every lead should have a clear next step. A CRM is an action system, not just a storage system.

title: The Eight-Part LeadProspectrr System
learningGoal: Understand the overall flow of LeadProspectrr and how the eight parts connect.

items.title: 1. Attract
items.description: Bring people to your business through websites, funnels, social media, email, reviews, advertising, prospecting, and referrals.

items.title: 2. Capture
items.description: Collect information through forms, surveys, calendar bookings, website chat, calls, text messages, imports, or manual entry.

items.title: 3. Organize
items.description: Store and classify people using contact records, tags, custom fields, notes, tasks, appointments, companies, and opportunities.

items.title: 4. Communicate
items.description: Manage supported communication such as email, SMS, phone calls, website chat, and connected social messages.

items.title: 5. Track
items.description: Use Opportunities and Pipelines to track possible sales, stages, values, statuses, and assigned team members.

items.title: 6. Follow Up
items.description: Use Workflows for repeatable actions such as emails, texts, reminders, tasks, tags, and internal notifications.

items.title: 7. Sell
items.description: Support the sales process with calendars, documents, contracts, invoices, payment links, products, and subscriptions.

items.title: 8. Report
items.description: Use dashboards and reports to review contacts, appointments, opportunities, pipeline value, payments, revenue, and other activity.

keyPoint: LeadProspectrr connects all eight parts of the customer journey. Understanding the flow helps you see how each feature supports the others.

actionSteps.title: Map Your Journey
actionSteps.description: Choose one service you sell and map its customer journey using the eight headings.

actionSteps.title: Identify Weak Points
actionSteps.description: Which of the eight parts is weakest in your current process?

actionSteps.title: Plan Improvements
actionSteps.description: Write down one action you could take to strengthen each weak point.

title: Contacts — The Center of the CRM
learningGoal: Understand how LeadProspectrr stores information about people and businesses.

items.title: Basic Information
items.description: Name, Email, Phone number, Company, Source. The foundation of every contact record.

items.title: Organization
items.description: Tags, Custom fields. Help you classify and segment contacts for targeted action.

items.title: Activity History
items.description: Notes, Tasks, Appointments, Conversations, Opportunities, Documents, Payments.

items.title: Sarah Downloads a Guide
items.description: LeadProspectrr creates Sarah as a contact, records the form she submitted, adds a tag, and starts a follow-up workflow.

items.title: Future Interactions
items.description: All future messages, appointments, opportunities, and payment activity are connected to Sarah's contact record.

keyPoint: The contact record is the center of everything. All activity, communication, and history connects back to the contact.

actionSteps.title: Open a Contact Record
actionSteps.description: Find one existing contact in LeadProspectrr and review their complete record.

actionSteps.title: Check for Completeness
actionSteps.description: Can you find their source, tags, notes, conversations, appointments, and opportunities?

actionSteps.title: Ask the Key Question
actionSteps.description: Could another team member understand what has happened and what should happen next?

quizzes.question: What is at the center of the LeadProspectrr CRM?
quizzes.explanation: The contact record is the center of the CRM. All activity, communication, appointments, and opportunities connect back to the contact.

quizzes.question: What information can a contact record include?

options.option_text: Name, email, phone, company, source, tags, custom fields, notes, tasks, appointments, conversations, opportunities, documents, and payments

quizzes.explanation: A complete contact record includes basic information, organization tags and fields, and full activity history including notes, tasks, appointments, conversations, opportunities, documents, and payments.

quizzes.question: Why is the contact record important?

options.option_text: All activity and history connects to it, creating a complete picture of the relationship

quizzes.explanation: The contact record is important because it connects all activity, communication, and history in one place, giving you a complete picture of each relationship.

title: Conversations and Calendars
learningGoal: Understand how communication and appointments connect back to the contact record.

items.title: Unified Communication
items.description: The Conversations area keeps supported messages together so communication is not scattered across separate systems.

items.title: Connected to Contacts
items.description: Every message is linked to the contact record, creating a complete communication history.

items.title: Booking Made Easy
items.description: Calendars allow prospects and clients to book available times: discovery calls, strategy sessions, coaching, consultations, onboarding, speaking enquiries, service appointments.

items.title: Automated Actions
items.description: Bookings can trigger confirmation messages, reminders, workflow actions, opportunity updates, and internal notifications.

keyPoint: Conversations and Calendars keep communication and appointments organized and connected to contacts. Everything is in one place.

actionSteps.title: Test Conversations
actionSteps.description: Using a test contact, send or record a message and check that it appears in their contact record.

actionSteps.title: Test Calendars
actionSteps.description: Book an appointment for a test contact and verify it appears in their contact record.

actionSteps.title: Review the Connection
actionSteps.description: Open the contact record and confirm both the message and appointment appear correctly.

quizzes.question: What does the Conversations area do?

options.option_text: Keeps supported messages together in one place

quizzes.explanation: The Conversations area unifies communication channels so messages are not scattered across separate systems. Everything connects to the contact record.

quizzes.question: What can calendar bookings trigger?

options.option_text: Confirmation messages, reminders, workflow actions, opportunity updates, and internal notifications

quizzes.explanation: Calendar bookings can trigger multiple automated actions: confirmations, reminders, workflows, opportunity updates, and notifications to your team.

quizzes.question: Why is it important that conversations and calendars connect to contacts?

options.option_text: It creates a complete history of all interactions in one place

quizzes.explanation: When conversations and calendars connect to contacts, you get a complete history of all interactions in one place. This helps with context and follow-up.

title: Opportunities and Pipelines
learningGoal: Understand the difference between a contact and a possible sale.

items.title: A Contact is the Person
items.description: A contact is the person or business you are communicating with. They may or may not be interested in buying.

items.title: An Opportunity is a Possible Sale
items.description: An opportunity is a possible sale connected to that person. It represents potential revenue.

items.title: Visual Sales Process
items.description: A pipeline is a visual representation of your sales process. It shows where each opportunity stands.

items.title: Example Pipeline
items.description: New Lead → Contacted → Appointment Booked → Proposal Sent → Decision Pending → Won/Lost

items.title: Key Questions
items.description: Who needs follow-up? Who has booked? Who has received a proposal? Which deals have gone quiet? What is the value of open opportunities?

keyPoint: A contact is the person. An opportunity is a possible sale. Pipelines help you track and manage the sales process visually.

actionSteps.title: Sketch Your Pipeline
actionSteps.description: Create or sketch one pipeline for your business with 4-6 stages.

actionSteps.title: Examples to Consider
actionSteps.description: Speaker: Speaking Enquiry → Qualification → Call → Proposal → Contract → Booked. Consultant: New Enquiry → Discovery Call → Proposal → Follow-Up → Won/Lost

actionSteps.title: Define Your Stages
actionSteps.description: Write down what happens at each stage and what moves someone to the next stage.

options.option_text: A contact is the person; an opportunity is a possible sale connected to that person
Contacts are free; opportunities cost money
Opportunities are not stored in LeadProspectrr

quizzes.explanation: A contact represents the person or business. An opportunity represents a possible sale connected to that contact. One contact can have multiple opportunities.

quizzes.question: What is a pipeline?

options.option_text: A visual representation of your sales process

quizzes.explanation: A pipeline visually represents your sales process with stages like New Lead, Contacted, Appointment Booked, Proposal Sent, and Won/Lost.

quizzes.question: What can pipelines help you see?

options.option_text: Who needs follow-up, who has booked, who received proposals, deal values, and won/lost sales

quizzes.explanation: Pipelines help you see who needs follow-up, who has booked appointments, who received proposals, which deals have gone quiet, the value of open opportunities, and which sales were won or lost.

title: Sites, Forms, Funnels, and Lead Capture
learningGoal: Understand how people enter the CRM and what happens after they take action.

items.title: Websites and Funnels
items.description: LeadProspectrr uses websites, funnels, landing pages, forms, surveys, chat widgets, and calendars to capture leads.

items.title: Example Lead Journey
items.description: Visitor lands on page → completes form → contact created → tag added → workflow begins → confirmation sent → appointment booked → opportunity created.

items.title: Page is Just the Beginning
items.description: The page itself is only the beginning. The value comes from what happens after the visitor takes action.

items.title: Focus on the Follow-Up
items.description: A beautiful page with no follow-up is worthless. A simple page with great follow-up is powerful.

keyPoint: The page is just the beginning. The real value comes from what happens after the visitor takes action—contact creation, tagging, workflows, and follow-up.

actionSteps.title: Pick One Form or Page
actionSteps.description: Choose one existing form or landing page in your LeadProspectrr account.

actionSteps.title: Audit the Follow-Up
actionSteps.description: Answer: What happens after submission? Is a contact created? Is the source recorded? Is a tag added? Does someone get notified?

actionSteps.title: Identify Gaps
actionSteps.description: Does follow-up begin? Should an opportunity be created? Fix any missing pieces.

quizzes.question: How do people enter LeadProspectrr?

options.option_text: Through websites, funnels, landing pages, forms, surveys, chat widgets, and calendars

quizzes.explanation: People enter LeadProspectrr through multiple channels: websites, funnels, landing pages, forms, surveys, chat widgets, and calendar bookings.

quizzes.question: What is the key idea about pages and funnels?

options.option_text: The page is just the beginning; the value comes from what happens after the visitor takes action

quizzes.explanation: The page or funnel is just the entry point. The real value comes from the follow-up: contact creation, tagging, workflows, notifications, and nurture sequences.

quizzes.question: What happens in a typical lead journey?

options.option_text: Visitor lands on page and nothing else happens
Visitor completes form, contact created, tag added, workflow begins, confirmation sent, appointment booked, opportunity created

quizzes.explanation: A typical lead journey includes: landing on page, completing form, contact creation, tagging, workflow trigger, confirmation email, appointment booking, and opportunity creation.

title: Workflows and Follow-Up
learningGoal: Understand how LeadProspectrr can automate repeatable actions.

items.title: Automatic Actions
items.description: A workflow is a set of automatic actions triggered by an event. They save time and ensure consistency.

items.title: Example Trigger
items.description: Trigger: A visitor completes a consultation form. This starts the workflow.

items.title: 1. Add a Tag
items.description: Organize and segment the contact based on their action.

items.title: 2. Send Confirmation Email
items.description: Let them know their request was received.

items.title: 3. Send Text Message
items.description: Reach them on their phone with important updates.

items.title: 4. Create Opportunity
items.description: Add them to your sales pipeline.

items.title: 5. Assign Contact
items.description: Give ownership to a specific team member.

items.title: 6. Create Task
items.description: Ensure someone follows up manually if needed.

items.title: 7. Wait
items.description: Pause before the next action.

items.title: 8. Check for Reply
items.description: See if they responded before sending more messages.

items.title: 9. Send Follow-Up
items.description: Continue the conversation if no reply was received.

items.title: 10. Stop Sequence
items.description: End the workflow when they book an appointment or complete the desired action.

keyPoint: Automate a clear process. If the manual process does not make sense, automating it will not fix it. Map the process first, then automate.

actionSteps.title: Choose a Repeatable Task
actionSteps.description: Pick one task you do repeatedly: replying to enquiries, sending reminders, following up after proposals, asking for reviews.

actionSteps.title: Write the Manual Process
actionSteps.description: Document each step you currently take manually.

actionSteps.title: Identify Automation Opportunities
actionSteps.description: Which steps could be automated? Which need human touch?

quizzes.question: What is a workflow?

options.option_text: A set of automatic actions triggered by an event

quizzes.explanation: A workflow is a series of automatic actions triggered by an event, such as form submission, tag application, or appointment booking.

quizzes.question: What can workflow actions include?

options.option_text: Adding tags, sending emails and texts, creating opportunities, assigning contacts, creating tasks, waiting, and checking for replies

quizzes.explanation: Workflows can perform many actions: add tags, send emails and texts, create opportunities, assign contacts, create tasks, wait, check for replies, and much more.

quizzes.question: What is the key idea about workflows?

options.option_text: Automate a clear process. If the manual process does not make sense, automating it will not fix it.

quizzes.explanation: The key is to automate a clear, working process. Map out the manual process first, then automate it. Automation amplifies good processes and bad processes alike.

title: Payments, Documents, and Reputation
learningGoal: Understand how LeadProspectrr supports the later stages of the customer journey.

items.title: Paperwork Management
items.description: Depending on your setup, you may manage proposals, documents, contracts, and electronic signatures inside LeadProspectrr.

items.title: Connected to Contacts
items.description: All documents are linked to the contact record for easy access and tracking.

items.title: Payment Tools
items.description: Payment tools may include invoices, payment links, products, order forms, and subscriptions.

items.title: Integrated with CRM
items.description: Payment activity is recorded on the contact record, giving you a complete financial history.

items.title: Review Process
items.description: A simple review process: Service completed → workflow sends review request → customer follows link → business monitors response → relationship continues.

items.title: Build Trust
items.description: Reviews and testimonials build trust with future prospects.

keyPoint: The customer journey does not end at the sale. Documents, payments, and reputation management support the complete relationship lifecycle.

actionSteps.title: Map Your Post-Sale Process
actionSteps.description: What happens after someone says yes to working with you?

actionSteps.title: List Requirements
actionSteps.description: What must they sign? What do they pay? What do they receive? What happens after delivery?

actionSteps.title: Plan Your Review Process
actionSteps.description: How will you ask for reviews? When? What workflow will trigger the request?

quizzes.question: What payment tools might LeadProspectrr include?

options.option_text: Invoices, payment links, products, order forms, and subscriptions

quizzes.explanation: LeadProspectrr can include various payment tools: invoices, payment links, products, order forms, and subscriptions, all connected to contact records.

quizzes.question: What is a simple review process?

options.option_text: Service completed → workflow sends review request → customer follows link → business monitors response → relationship continues

quizzes.explanation: A good review process uses workflows to automatically request reviews after service completion, making it easy for customers to leave feedback.

quizzes.question: Why are documents connected to contacts important?

options.option_text: They provide easy access to proposals, contracts, and agreements in one place

quizzes.explanation: When documents are connected to contacts, you have easy access to all proposals, contracts, and agreements in one place, creating a complete record of the relationship.

title: Dashboards and Reporting
learningGoal: Understand how reporting helps you see what is happening in the business.

items.title: Contact Activity
items.description: Contacts, conversations, calls, appointments.

items.title: Sales Metrics
items.description: Opportunities, pipeline value, conversion activity.

items.title: Financial Data
items.description: Payments, revenue, outstanding invoices.

items.title: Key Business Questions
items.description: How many new leads? Where did they come from? How many booked appointments? How many opportunities are open? Where are deals getting stuck? How much potential business is in the pipeline? How many sales were won? What revenue was collected?

items.title: Dashboard Shows What Is Happening
items.description: A dashboard shows what is happening. It does not replace a clear sales and follow-up process.

keyPoint: Dashboards and reports show what is happening in your business. Use them to make informed decisions, but remember they complement—do not replace—your sales process.

actionSteps.title: Choose Three Numbers
actionSteps.description: Pick three metrics that would help you make better decisions each week.

actionSteps.title: Plan Your Response
actionSteps.description: Decide what action you would take if each number was too low.

actionSteps.title: Set Up Dashboard
actionSteps.description: Configure your LeadProspectrr dashboard to show these key metrics.

title: Build Your First Connected CRM Journey
learningGoal: Bring the main areas together into one working customer journey.

items.title: The Complete Flow
items.description: Visitor reaches landing page → completes form → contact created → tag added → workflow sends confirmation → opportunity created → contact books appointment → reminders sent → consultation takes place → proposal sent → opportunity marked won/lost → next follow-up begins → review request sent → dashboard reviewed.

items.title: 1. Add or Import Contacts
items.description: Start with the people you already know.

items.title: 2. Create Contact Fields
items.description: Set up custom fields you need for your business.

items.title: 3. Create Useful Tags
items.description: Organize contacts by source, interest, or status.

items.title: 4. Set Up One Pipeline
items.description: Create a simple sales pipeline with 4-6 stages.

items.title: 5. Connect One Calendar
items.description: Set up booking for consultations or discovery calls.

items.title: 6. Create One Lead Form
items.description: Build a simple form to capture new leads.

items.title: 7. Create Confirmation Message
items.description: Set up a thank-you email for form submissions.

items.title: 8. Create Follow-Up Workflow
items.description: Build a simple workflow for new leads.

items.title: 9. Test the Full Journey
items.description: Use your own email to test everything works.

items.title: 10. Review Results
items.description: Check your dashboard and make improvements.

keyPoint: A working six-step process is more useful than a complicated twenty-step process that nobody uses. Start simple, test thoroughly, then improve.

actionSteps.title: Map Your Journey
actionSteps.description: Choose one real customer journey and map it using the eight LeadProspectrr parts.

actionSteps.title: Answer the Questions
actionSteps.description: How do they enter? What is captured? How are they organized? What communication happens? When do they become an opportunity? What pipeline stage? What follow-up? How do they book? How do they buy? What happens after? What will you measure?

actionSteps.title: Build and Test
actionSteps.description: Use your own email address to test the complete journey from form to pipeline.

quizzes.question: What is the recommended beginner setup order?

options.option_text: Contacts, fields, tags, pipeline, calendar, form, confirmation, workflow, test, review

quizzes.explanation: The recommended order is: add contacts, create fields, create tags, set up pipeline, connect calendar, create form, create confirmation, create workflow, test, and review.

quizzes.question: Why test with your own email?

options.option_text: To experience the journey as a real lead would and catch any issues

quizzes.explanation: Testing with your own email lets you experience the complete journey as a real lead would, helping you catch issues before real prospects encounter them.

quizzes.question: What is better: a simple six-step process or a complex twenty-step process?

options.option_text: A working six-step process is more useful than a complicated process nobody uses

quizzes.explanation: A simple working process is always better than a complex one that is too difficult to use. Start simple, get it working, then add complexity only if needed.
